evidence.location: line 7 (§0) and line 41 (§6), against line 29 (§4 DB1)
evidence.observation: §0 requires "Bound counterexample rows independently of scan size" and §6 only requires "Record work counters and the first refusal where limits apply", while the DB1 deliverable is to "expose violating antecedent bindings"; no clause states that the public boundary must distinguish a complete binding set from one truncated by the row bound.

concerns.recommendation: Add a binding-design rule that a bounded counterexample result carries an explicit truncation signal or suppressed-row count at the public boundary, and make DB3's verdict, affected-binding and coverage comparison account for it on both the native and DuckDB sides.
concerns.title: Bounded counterexample rows lack a caller-visible truncation signal

evidence.observation: §0 says "Use a read-only engine transaction" and "test both sides of every refusal", but the DB2 verification at §9 only schedules "introduce a duplicate in a read-only database snapshot and compare against a checked materialized population from the same rows; also test missing projection, NULL, duplicate input and incompatible type" — no case demonstrates that a write attempted through the checking path is actually refused or prevented.

concerns.recommendation: Schedule an explicit safety test that a mutation attempted on the read-only engine path (writable connection rejected, or INSERT/DDL refused during checking) fails, applying the plan's own both-sides-of-every-refusal rule to the read-only control itself.
concerns.title: Read-only safety claim has no scheduled negative test

evidence.observation: §6 enumerates the controls "Use a read-only engine transaction. Validate relation identifiers and projection types before executing a rule. Bound counterexample rows independently of scan size" — the bound covers output rows only, and §2's requirement to "Exercise a real read-only database" carries no stated memory, thread, temp-spill or statement-time budget for the database side, leaving scan work unbounded by design.

concerns.recommendation: State a DuckDB-side work control (memory_limit, threads, or an equivalent budget plus a refusal path when exceeded) in §6 and record it wherever work counters are recorded.
concerns.title: No memory or runtime control for unbounded database scans

evidence.observation: §5 assigns "DB3 records engine and adapter versions" — versions are recorded at the end of the milestone, with no rule that all parity evidence across DB1-DB3 come from one pinned engine and adapter version set.

concerns.recommendation: Pin the DuckDB engine and adapter versions (lockfile or recorded pins) before DB3 parity runs so the recorded versions describe every observation rather than only the final state.
concerns.title: Engine and adapter versions are recorded after the fact, not pinned for parity evidence

evidence.observation: §4 DB3's exit criterion is "Compare native and database verdicts over the same records, including missing tables, uncovered roles and bounded source keys" and lists both #327 and #330, but §9's explicit DB3 recipe only names "run the #330 good and bad populations against native GND and the generated DuckDB program. Compare verdict, affected binding and coverage"; the missing-table, uncovered-role and bounded-source-key differential cases and the #327 reproduction are carried only by the generic sentence at line 55 ("use the issue reproduction and the criterion in §4 as an acceptance pair").

concerns.recommendation: When the DB3 spec is drafted, enumerate the missing-table, uncovered-role and bounded-source-key differential cases and the #327 reproduction explicitly in its acceptance list so the §4 criterion is discharged by named cases rather than by inheritance from a general rule.
concerns.title: DB3 verification recipe omits the differential edge cases named in its exit criterion

response.summary: The plan bytes hash to the requested digest and its intake claims check out against code (an existential consequent is refused in src/gnd/export/pyrel_rules.py:395-400). Phasing, owner gates and the issue-to-phase mapping in §4 are internally consistent with the DB1 spec. The concerns below are hardening and completeness: bounded counterexample rows lack a caller-visible truncation signal, the read-only control has no scheduled negative test, database-side scan work has no memory or runtime budget, engine versions are recorded after the fact rather than pinned, and the DB3 recipe leaves its own differential edge cases to a generic acceptance rule.
